headline: Brain organoids track time over five years
standfirst: Scientists grew human brain cells in a lab to see how they mature on their own.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Researchers grew human brain organoids for five years to see if they mature on their own.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The cells were kept in culture to mimic how a natural brain develops over time.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: It proves brain cells follow internal biological programs even outside a human body.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Future studies on how these organoids record time without a full organism present.

caption:
Scientists have found that human brain organoids can record the passage of time over multiple years in a lab.

This study published in Nature shows that brain cells continue to mature using their own internal biological programs. This development happened entirely outside the context of a living human organism.
